newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario says balanced budget plan on track.
newsitem.headline: Ontario says balanced budget plan on track.

text.p: The Ontario government on Thursday said its fiscal 1996/97 budget deficit target of C$8.173 billion is unchanged and the province is on track for a balanced budget by 2000/2001.
"I am pleased to report that the economic and fiscal plan that this government has put in place is on track," Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves said in his mid-term economic and fiscal outlook.
Eves said the Ontario economy's improved performance will not require the government to use a C$650 million reserve set aside in the 1996 budget.
Eves said Ontario's economy was forecast to show real growth of 2.3 percent this year, up from 1.9 percent forecast in his budget last spring.

"With improved economic performance, I would expect that we will not need to use the C$650 million reserve...unless some unanticipated risk such as an economic downturn occurs to require its use," Eves said.

He said the second stage of the government's promised cut in personal income taxes would take effect as planned on January 1, 1997. He said half of the government's promised 30 percent tax cut would have been delivered at that time.
Ontario's ruling Conservatives swept to power in June, 1995 promising to balance the budget by the turn of the century and cut income taxes to spur a sluggish economy.
Eves has already detailed spending cuts totalling about C$6 billion. He was expected to detail another C$3 billion in program cuts in a mini-budget before Christmas.

But Eves cancelled the mini-budget on Wednesday, saying that the government is still awaiting reports from special government advisor David Crombie. Opposition critics on Thursday speculated that the government is having trouble reconciling the tax cuts with its balanced budget plan.
Some analysts have said Ontario's balanced budget plan could be derailed if the economy of Canada's most-populous province weakened significantly over the next four years.

"An economic downturn anytime before the projected balanced budget date in 2000-01 is a significant risk to the government's plan," Dominion Bond Rating Service Ltd said in a report released earlier this week.
If Ontario's gross domestic product growth is one percentage point below forecast each year through 2000-01, an extra C$2.8 billion in program spending would have to be cut, DBRS said.
